messages.content:
You are an expert synthetic chemist planning experiments to maximise reaction yield.
Each experiment chooses one option for every variable listed. You will see the results
of experiments already run. Choose the next batch to find the highest-yield conditions
in as few experiments as possible. Use chemical knowledge (ligand and base effects,
substrate reactivity, solvent effects) and the observed results. Balance exploiting
good regions with testing informative new combinations. Never repeat an experiment.
Return JSON only.

Pd-catalysed Buchwald-Hartwig amination of 1-bromo-4-(trifluoromethyl)benzene with 4-methylaniline; choose the ligand, base and isoxazole additive.

Variables and options:
ligand:
L1: tBuBrettPhos [SMILES CC(C)C(C=C(C(C)C)C=C1C(C)C)=C1C2=C(P(C(C)(C)C)C(C)(C)C)C(OC)=CC=C2OC]

L3: XPhos [SMILES CC(C)C(C=C(C(C)C)C=C1C(C)C)=C1C2=C(P(C3CCCCC3)C4CCCCC4)C=CC=C2]

picks.reason: This combines the best observed ligand, base, and additive, while testing whether their individually favorable effects give the highest yield together.
A9 performs well with L2 under B1, so testing B3 isolates whether the strongest observed base further improves this combination.
This checks whether the strong A9 response with B3 extends to L3 despite its weaker result with B1.
A9 is consistently favorable and this tests whether the strong phosphazene base can outperform B3 with L1.
This compares B2 with the leading B3 condition while holding the best observed ligand and additive fixed.
A13 is a positional isomer of the leading A9 additive and can reveal whether the methyl and ester positions control the benefit.
A8 is another positional isomer of A9 and tests whether the isoxazole substitution pattern is responsible for A9's strong result.
This tests whether an isoxazole-3-carboxylate retains activity without A9's methyl substituent.
This evaluates the alternate 4-carboxylate placement against the favorable A9 additive under the leading catalyst conditions.
A20 tests whether a 5-carboxylate additive remains effective with a smaller methyl ester instead of A9's ethyl ester.
The methoxy-substituted carboxylate probes whether additional electron donation can improve on the A9 additive.
The furyl-substituted isoxazole tests whether an extended heteroaryl group can outperform the simpler A9 additive.
The thienyl analogue of A21 probes a different heteroaryl effect while retaining the ester-bearing isoxazole scaffold.
The dimethylisoxazole tests whether a compact, electron-rich additive can help without the ester group present in A9.
This tests a simple methylisoxazole under the leading conditions to assess whether A9's ester group is necessary for its benefit.
A14 gave moderate results with B1, so the leading B3 base may reveal a more favorable effect from its phenyl-substituted scaffold.
A11 showed moderate activity with B1 and merits testing with B3 to determine whether the pyrrolyl substituent is beneficial.
This tests a simple phenylisoxazole additive under the leading catalyst conditions as a less substituted alternative to A9.
The 3-phenylisoxazole isomer tests whether phenyl placement on the isoxazole ring influences additive performance.
The difluorophenyl analogue probes whether an electron-poor aryl substituent can improve additive performance over unsubstituted phenyl.
